feed.subtitle: Research papers and global crypto regulation, at a glance
feed.rights: Explanations and summaries are generated by AI from the original text. Dates, rates and amounts are checked against the source, but errors are still possible, so always rely on the original. Nothing here is legal, tax or investment advice.

entry.title: Modeling and Calibrating Climate-Related Credit Risk Under Emissions Trading Systems
entry.summary: Modelling and Calibration of Climate-Related Credit Risk Under the Emissions Trading System arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper builds a structural model in which firms choose emissions from several energy sources under an anticipated carbon price, with the realized price clearing each sector-region carbon market. It proves the equilibrium carbon price exists, characterizes when the emissions cap binds, and derives each firm's optimal emissions in feedback form. In a linearized case the carbon price is deterministic and default probability has an explicit form. Calibrated to 35 European power producers under the EU ETS, the model reproduces the average EU Allowance price level for 2018 to 2024.

entry.title: A graph-informed deep factor model for profiting from temporary price gaps between similar stocks
entry.summary: Graph-Informed Deep Factor Model for Statistical Arbitrage arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes a nonlinear single-factor model, GIDF, for daily statistical arbitrage in equities. It reconstructs a latent network of cross-sectional return dependencies left after removing the dominant eigenmodes of the correlation matrix, then combines it with firm characteristics and macroeconomic variables via a signed-edge graph attention mechanism. In an empirical study of daily U.S. equities from 2015 to 2024, GIDF reports an out-of-sample Sharpe ratio of 1.78 and outperforms classical factor models and state-of-the-art deep learning methods.

entry.title: Time consistency of risk measures: an infimal cocycle property
entry.summary: Time-consistency of cash-subadditive risk measures: The infimal cocycle property arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper characterizes time-consistency for convex, cash-subadditive dynamic risk measures through their minimal penalty. The dual variables are conditional sub-probability densities that can factorize across an intermediate date in several ways. The authors introduce an infimal cocycle property, where the penalty is the infimum over all such factorizations, and show it is equivalent to time-consistency with the infimum attained.

entry.title: Rank-size analysis of optimal portfolio weights and reverse-engineering their generating model
entry.summary: Rank-size analysis of optimal portfolio weights with a reverse-engineering application arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper uses rank-size analysis to study the shape of optimal portfolio weights across four selection models: Global Minimum-Variance, minimum-CVaR, Risk Parity, and Most Diversified Portfolio. Seven rank-size functional forms are fitted to sorted weights over rolling windows and compared using goodness-of-fit measures and Cumulative Second-order ε-Stochastic Dominance, with empirical application to major equity indices. The authors also feed the calibrated parameters into a Random Forest classifier to identify the generating model. The parameters separate minimum-risk from risk-diversification strategies and identify Risk Parity and Most Diversified portfolios, while Global Minimum-Variance and minimum-CVaR are hard to distinguish.

entry.title: Will AI Replace Junior Staff? How Task Complexity Lowers Automation Risk
entry.summary: Will AI Replace Juniors? How Task Complexity Reduces Automation Risk arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This study uses a pre-registered survey experiment with managers from 1,435 German firms in the information economy and manufacturing. Managers were randomly assigned to consider either standardised tasks or complex tasks requiring professional judgement and independent problem-solving. Compared with standardised tasks, complex tasks reduced willingness to use AI instead of hiring entry-level staff by 0.54 points on a five-point scale and raised the importance of human oversight by 0.15 points.

entry.title: Budget, readout or reasoning: where small reasoning models lose value in auction bidding
entry.summary: Budget, Readout or Reasoning? Where Small Reasoning Models Lose Value in Auction Bidding arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The study gives six open reasoning models of 4B to 14B parameters win-probability curves from eBay closing prices and a simulated advertising market (AuctionNet), then scores their bids on held-out auctions against an exact calculator. The models themselves cause two kinds of losses: they overlook the best option even when their own reasoning ranks it first, and their wrong answers tend toward the highest bid available. Token caps that truncate reasoning and answering before the reasoning block is closed also reduce value, while closing the block first substantially improves results.

entry.title: Cleaning correlation matrices with external group information: the MaxVar estimator
entry.summary: Cleaning correlation matrices with external information: the Maximum Variance estimator arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper proposes the Maximum Variance (MaxVar) estimator, which corrects the eigenvectors of an empirical correlation matrix using a grouping of assets such as asset classes or regions. It is a factor model with about n parameters and stays positive definite even when observations are fewer than assets. Applied to 47 futures from 1993 to 2018, the risk parity portfolio built with MaxVar achieves a higher Sharpe ratio than rotationally invariant and empirical estimators, with the advantage growing as the estimation window shortens.

entry.title: How LLM Agents Are Reshaping Financial Knowledge Graphs: A Survey
entry.summary: How LLM Agents Reshape Financial Knowledge Graphs: A Survey arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This is the first survey on how LLM agents change the building, maintenance, and use of financial knowledge graphs. It proposes a taxonomy covering knowledge graph construction, temporal evolution, verification, reconciliation and admission, adaptive acquisition, and graph usage. The survey finds that agents can recover evidence missed in an initial search and revise records as new information arrives. It identifies three open questions: judging whether evidence is sufficient for a financial decision, determining which earlier conclusions must change after a correction, and identifying relationships and rules reusable in new graphs or domains.

entry.title: Worth the Wait? Response Time, Streaming and Judgments of AI Chatbot Answers
entry.summary: Worth the Wait? How Response Time and Streaming Shape Judgments of Generative AI Answers and Chatbot Engagement arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper examines how the speed and display style of answers from LLM chatbots affect user judgments. It analyzes blind votes from the French government chatbot arena compar:IA, slower streamed answers caused by provider congestion, and everyday ChatGPT replies in the WildChat dataset. The same text won more votes when streamed as it was written than when shown at once, and slower replies made users less likely to ask follow-up questions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors separate answer delivery (streaming versus cached replay) from blind votes, reporting three natural-data tests; streamed text won more votes and delays reduced follow-up questions.

entry.title: Hedging price and volatility risk with deep reinforcement learning, from simulation to market data
entry.summary: Delta-Vega Hedging with Deep Reinforcement Learning: From Simulation to Reality arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning method that hedges both price and volatility risk by trading the underlying asset and a longer-dated option under discrete trading and transaction costs. The agent is trained with PPO on synthetic data from a stochastic volatility model, using only market-observable state variables. In simulation, PPO matches the Delta-Vega benchmark at baseline costs and outperforms it as costs rise. On historical S&P 500 option data, the two-instrument strategies roughly halve the profit-and-loss dispersion of Delta hedging, and PPO shows lower profit-and-loss volatility than Delta-Vega.

entry.title: Downside-risk portfolio models: semivariance and semivolatility unified
entry.summary: Semivariance and Semivolatility in Portfolio Selection: A Unified Framework for Downside-Risk Portfolio Models arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies downside risk in portfolio selection, comparing semivariance and its square root, semivolatility. The authors classify models by the positive homogeneity degree of the risk measure in the weights and give a non-degeneracy condition for long-only downside risk under three thresholds. They run a rolling-window out-of-sample backtest of seventeen long-only strategies on Dow Jones and Nasdaq-100 total-return data, testing differences with block-bootstrap inference.

entry.title: Dynamic multi-attribute group decision-making using fractional-order stochastic dominance
entry.summary: Dynamic stochastic multi-attribute group decision-making based on fractional-order stochastic dominance criteria arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper proposes a dynamic group decision-making model for choosing among alternatives under uncertainty. It uses fractional-order stochastic dominance criteria, which are finer than integer-order ones, to compare alternatives. The model also works for decision-makers whose utility functions are not concave everywhere, and it lets attributes and alternatives be added or removed across decision periods. Numerical examples and comparisons are presented to show its effectiveness and robustness.

entry.title: A kernel-based framework for solving linear operator equations, including option pricing examples
entry.summary: A Kernel Framework for Linear Operator Equations arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper proposes a unified method that embeds linear operator equations into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) and solves them in the regularized least-squares sense at finitely many collocation points. The solution is a finite linear combination of operator-induced representers, obtained from a single linear system, and sensitivities follow by direct differentiation. To reduce cost for large collocation sets, the authors introduce a Nyström approximation based on subsampling the representers. Numerical examples cover ordinary, partial, and partial integro-differential equations, including multi-asset and jump-diffusion option pricing.

entry.title: Training decision models to simulate human survey respondents
entry.summary: Training decision models for simulating human respondents arXiv · Nov 24, 2026Researchers increasingly use large language models as synthetic respondents in market research, conjoint analysis, and experiments, but synthetic choice data from off-the-shelf models biases econometric inference. The paper trains decision models (System One architectures) on historical respondent-level choice microdata by conditional maximum likelihood, before inference and without target-study data. Across four held-out studies from new domains, training lowers treatment-effect error by 22% to 89%, and a small trained model outperforms a much larger off-the-shelf model on three of the four studies.

entry.title: AI Coding Assistants and Tech Hiring: How GitHub Copilot Affects Labor Demand
entry.summary: AI-Assisted Programming and Labor Demand arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies how firms adopted GitHub Copilot, an AI coding assistant, across 5,414 multinational firms that account for 38% of the U.S. programming workforce. The authors use firms' predetermined software procurement cycles as a natural experiment to identify causal effects. After one year, adoption reduced quarterly technical hiring by 29%, with no effect on separations or overall technical headcount. The slowdown is concentrated in junior technical roles with the most coding work, and firms shift demand toward more experienced workers and roles combining coding with broader design responsibilities. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors use a natural experiment across 5,414 firms to causally estimate AI coding assistants' effect on technical hiring, with broad labor-market implications.

entry.title: Critical step size of SGD for a linear neuron, and the role of input spectrum
entry.summary: Critical step size of stochastic gradient descent for a linear neuron: an exact solution and the role of the input spectrum arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper studies online stochastic gradient descent for a single linear neuron in a teacher-student setting with Gaussian inputs of arbitrary covariance. It solves the closed linear recursion for the mean-square errors exactly and proves convergence holds if and only if the step size is below a critical value, given by an explicit scalar equation involving all eigenvalues of the input covariance. The critical step size is governed by the effective rank of the input covariance rather than the number of parameters, and it grows linearly with mini-batch size until saturating beyond the effective rank.

entry.title: CCFinance: Rebuilding Financial News Samples from Web Archives
entry.summary: CCFinance: Reconstructing Financial News Samples from Web Archives arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper presents CCFinance, a resource that reconstructs financial news samples from public Common Crawl News records. From 14.8 million English records in Fine News, it identifies 5.22 million consistently dated articles with issuer links and evaluates link and story-focus accuracy against blinded model judgments. Three reimplementations illustrate its use for volatility tracking, bank networks, and overnight returns.

entry.title: Wasserstein Penalty as a Diversification Constraint in Long-Only Mean-Variance Portfolios
entry.summary: Wasserstein Penalisation as an Endogenous Breadth Constraint in Penalised Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper studies long-only mean-variance portfolio selection with a Wasserstein robustness penalty. Under this penalised formulation, the robustness radius effectively controls only the portfolio's effective breadth, the number of holdings. Tests on fourteen A-share panels show that capping breadth at the robust portfolio's historical level recovers most of its gain, whereas a fixed breadth target recovers much less.

entry.title: Political views and prediction market participation: large bets converge, small bets diverge
entry.summary: Political Orientation and Participation in Prediction Markets: Large Stakes Converge, Small Stakes Diverge arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper analyzes about 1.14 billion transaction records from the Polymarket prediction platform, covering over 3.1 million wallets and 764,000 events, using a bipartite user-event network. It finds that 1% of events account for 64% of transaction volume and 1% of wallets account for 79.2% of financial participation. Focusing on the 2024 U.S. presidential election, it compares users who bet only on a Trump win with those who bet only on a Harris win, finding that large investors allocate capital across topics more similarly than small investors.

entry.title: Discrete-time model approximating rough Hawkes-Heston option pricing
entry.summary: Marked INAR model and the rough Hawkes--Heston limit arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper develops a discrete-time Monte Carlo algorithm for the rough Hawkes-Heston model, built on a nearly unstable marked integer-valued autoregressive process and implemented with a block FFT scheme. It proves joint convergence in law of the spot variance, log price and marked point measure to the rough Hawkes-Heston limits, and convergence of European, arithmetic Asian and down-and-out put option prices to their continuously monitored values. Numerical experiments show one-year implied volatility smiles approaching the continuous affine reference across four roughness levels, and demonstrate the algorithm's efficiency.

entry.title: Gated Payoff-Weighted Net Profit Maximization for Online Portfolio Selection with Transaction Costs
entry.summary: Gated Payoff-Weighted Net Profit Maximization For Online Portfolio Selection With Transaction Costs arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies online portfolio selection under transaction costs. It finds that forecasts from the AOLNPM strategy, which uses Adaptive Online Moving Average predictions, overstate realized returns. The authors add a gate that learns, for each asset, how much of the forecast to use, and treat it as an asset-specific cost threshold. On nine datasets at a 0.1% transaction cost rate, the method reaches 5.9 times AOLNPM's geometric mean wealth and outperforms it on every dataset.

entry.title: Project financing in vanishing forests: Do investors care about nature protection?
entry.summary: Project financing in vanishing forests: Do investors care about nature protection? arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper links 9,037 project-loan pairs across 115 countries to examine whether bank loan spreads reflect projects' proximity to protected areas, surrounding forest loss, and lenders' nature policies. Lenders price protected-area proximity only when they have explicit nature risk policies, especially within 1.5 km of the project. The authors conclude that nature risk is partly priced in project finance, but this is not a strong incentive to deter significant harm to nature.

entry.title: Knowing When to Refuse: Conformal Confidence Estimation for Text-to-SQL
entry.summary: Know When to Abstain: Conformal Confidence Estimation for Text-to-SQL arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper addresses Text-to-SQL systems that run successfully but answer the wrong question. A generator LLM writes and executes queries, while a separate critic LLM judges them, and a Random Forest fuses these scores with other confidence signals. Two calibration steps, a Learn-then-Test threshold and a conformal p-value, provide finite-sample guarantees on the error rate of accepted queries and on false abstentions. On Spider, the method keeps the error among accepted queries within a set risk budget while accepting about half of queries.

entry.title: Are Candlestick Charts Enough? Whether Technical Indicators Add Economic Value to Stock Return Prediction
entry.summary: Do Candlestick Charts Suffice? The Incremental Economic Value of Technical Indicators in Stock Return Prediction arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper uses daily data from 1,707 Chinese A-share stocks over 2013 to 2025, encoding candlestick charts, trading volume, and seven common technical indicators as multi-channel images for prediction models. Out-of-sample tests from 2021 to 2025 find that OHLC, trading volume, and each indicator group alone yield significantly positive high-minus-low returns and factor-adjusted alphas. OHLC-only specifications generally perform best under nonlinear models. Adding the technical indicators to OHLC does not systematically improve these results.

entry.title: The Rise of AI Agents and Labor Demand: Economy-Wide Evidence on Job Postings
entry.summary: The Rise of Agents and the Labor Market arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies how agentic AI affects labor demand, combining about two quadrillion tokens of realized AI usage from OpenRouter with full text of 34.8 million U.S. job postings from Lightcast. Firm exposure is measured by how U.S. public firms' stock returns comove with weekly aggregate agentic AI token consumption. A one-standard-deviation rise in exposure predicts 2.11% and 3.20% lower job posting growth over six and nine months. An event study around the Claude Code 2.0 release shows a 4.73% decline, concentrated in non-senior jobs. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors use realized agentic AI token data and job postings to study labor demand effects economy-wide, finding declines in posting growth concentrated in non-senior roles.

entry.title: Strategic Repayment and Hidden Fragility in Financial Networks
entry.summary: Liquidity Commitments and Strategic Settlement in Financial Networks arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper shows that a financial network in which every bank pays in full can still admit a self-fulfilling settlement freeze under the same balance-sheet fundamentals, so full repayment alone does not prove equilibrium uniqueness or robustness. It derives this from a precautionary liquidity choice in which banks delay feasible payments to insure against an interim funding need, weighing settlement-discipline costs against the value of retained cash. The authors also characterise network amplification and conditions for coexisting equilibria, and separate payment timing from ultimate default.

entry.title: Monitoring Which Loans Prepay, Not How Many: Level-Invariant, Anytime-Valid Checks for Deployed Mortgage Risk Models
entry.summary: Which Loans, Not How Many: Exactly Level-Invariant, Anytime-Valid Monitoring of Deployed Risk Models arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper proposes methods for monitoring deployed mortgage prepayment risk models so that a refinancing wave, which changes prepayment counts, does not distort the results. By conditioning a logistic model on the monthly prepayment count, the intercept is removed from the likelihood of which loans prepay. The authors introduce a fixed-start slope product test, a restarted level sum, a confidence sequence, and a restart-intersection rule, and evaluate them on Freddie Mac loan data.

entry.title: Model doubt, risk aversion, and when investors stop trading
entry.summary: Model Doubt, Risk Aversion, and the Threshold for Trading: A Geometry of Pricing Measures arXiv · Nov 21, 2026The paper asks how much doubt about a model an investor can hold before they stop trading, measuring model doubt with Kullback-Leibler divergence. In a finite one-period market, the investor holds no risky asset once this doubt reaches the smallest divergence of a pricing measure from their model. The authors illustrate the results with a century of U.S. data.

entry.title: Rebuilding risk preferences from observed data
entry.summary: Reconstructing risk preferences from data arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies how to reconstruct a risk measure from a finite dataset of contingent claims and their evaluations. It gives necessary and sufficient conditions for such a dataset to be compatible with a risk measure, and a reconstruction formula called the universal risk measure. The method is extended to monotone risk measures with sharp Lipschitz constants, and a numerical application to European options is presented.

entry.title: Do physics-inspired inputs improve neural covariance forecasts? A leakage-free walk-forward study of DJIA intraday data
entry.summary: Do Econophysics-Inspired Inputs Improve Neural Covariance Forecasting? A Leakage-Free Walk-Forward Study of Intraday DJIA Data arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper tests whether econophysics tools, including Random Matrix Theory, Tsallis tail indices and Hawkes intensities, improve neural network forecasts of one-day-ahead asset covariance. It uses 1-minute data from 29 Dow Jones Industrial Average constituents over 545 trading days, evaluated with a nested walk-forward design of 11 folds and 231 out-of-sample days. Neural models beat static covariance estimators but show no statistically significant gain over HAR-RV or LSTM benchmarks, and the physics-inspired features make no measurable contribution.

entry.title: Accountable AI delegation in banking: identity, controls, and recovery
entry.summary: Accountable AI Delegation in Banking: Identity, Commitment Controls, Decision Evidence and Recovery arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper specifies a banking delegation contract that checks current authority, a shared payment cap, and whether eligible instruments can cover losses before an AI-assisted payment is committed. It records the payment, recovery demands, and outcome in one atomic transition. Paired examples show what reviewers need to assess mandate conformance, and tests report results on rule reversal, reused state, pooled recovery capacity, and record retention. Survey responses and an insurance example are also included.

entry.title: Risk sharing for losses with infinite mean
entry.summary: Risk sharing for background risk models with infinite mean arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies how risk sharing affects positively dependent losses with infinite mean, using background risk models. Under both linear and conditional mean risk sharing, it shows that sharing such losses can increase risk in the usual stochastic order. The results cover multivariate models such as Pareto-Clayton and Fréchet-Gumbel, and include stochastic dominance comparisons between diversified portfolios.

entry.title: Nonlinear Shrinkage for Higher Moments in Large Portfolios
entry.summary: Nonlinear Shrinkage for Higher Moments Estimation in Large Portfolios arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper addresses the noisy estimation of higher-order portfolio moments, such as coskewness and cokurtosis, for large portfolios. It introduces tensor-decomposition-based filters that extend cross-validated covariance cleaning and the Average Oracle method to even-order co-moment tensors. Using historical Russell 1000 constituent returns, the authors report that the filters reduce out-of-sample estimation error for correlation and cokurtosis tensors compared with sample estimators. The improvements also lower errors in portfolio volatility and kurtosis estimates.

entry.title: Trust and lottery-related anomalies: how social trust shapes the pricing of lottery-like stocks
entry.summary: Trust and Lottery-Related Anomalies arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper examines whether social trust affects the pricing of lottery-like stocks. Using 8,875 firms across 49 US states from 1996 to 2018, with MAX as a proxy for lottery-like characteristics, it finds the MAX effect concentrated in high-trust regions and weak or absent in low-trust regions. The trust effect is stronger in areas with lower education or income levels.

entry.title: Are Calibrated Decision Models Still Calibrated in Markets? Geolocated News, Markov Switching and a Nasdaq-100 Allocation Model
entry.summary: Are Calibrated Decision Models Calibrated on Markets? Geolocated News, Markov Switching and a System One Model for Nasdaq-100 Allocation arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The study asks each Friday whether the Nasdaq-100 will close lower four weeks later, comparing a two-regime Markov-switching model, the Jev model reading weekly headlines and geolocated news features, and their combination. Raw Jev overestimates declines, averaging 0.48 against an observed frequency of 0.38. Shifting its prior to the historical base rate sharply reduces calibration error.

entry.title: Held-to-Maturity Accounting: Hidden Losses and Systemic Fragility
entry.summary: Held-to-Maturity Accounting: Hidden Losses and Systemic Fragility arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper examines how accounting-induced opacity affects systemic risk in banking systems. The authors build a model in which banks hold correlated interest rate sensitive assets and are linked through an endogenous interbank network. They find that Held-to-Maturity (HTM) accounting amplifies systemic risk by delaying loss recognition, letting losses accumulate and synchronize across institutions. When losses are realized under liquidity stress, correlated exposures and network linkages generate nonlinear increases in defaults.

entry.title: Error analysis for numerically approximating quantile hedging
entry.summary: Error analysis for the numerical approximation of the quantile hedging problem arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies numerical approximations of quantile hedging in complete linear markets with Markovian diffusion dynamics, formulated as stochastic control on an augmented state whose probability martingale is constrained to [0,1]. The authors combine control truncation with piecewise-constant policy time-stepping and stop controls at the boundary to preserve the constraint, deriving explicit value-function error bounds. Experiments in Black–Scholes and Lipschitz local-volatility models illustrate the correction and the decrease in pricing errors under grid refinement.

entry.title: A Solvency II-based framework for pricing structural longevity risk using an affine mortality model
entry.summary: A Solvency II-Based Framework for Pricing Structural Longevity Risk under an Affine Mortality Model arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a pricing framework for structural longevity risk in incomplete markets, combining the Solvency II Cost-of-Capital principle behind the Risk Margin with a continuous-time affine mortality model driven by a latent longevity factor. It derives analytical expressions for the asymmetry and Value-at-Risk of the one-year discounted Best Estimate variation under a Gaussian affine specification. The authors compare a trend-based stress with a mortality-level stress and a VaR-based capital assessment. A numerical application using Belgian mortality data finds that the mortality-level stress yields substantially larger scenario-based capital-cost measures.

entry.title: Distributional Deep Hedging: learning profit-and-loss distributions before applying risk preferences
entry.summary: Distributional Deep Hedging arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper proposes distributional deep hedging, which learns the distribution of hedging profit and loss through its quantiles and applies the risk preference afterwards as a weight on those quantiles. It characterises the preferences that admit this representation, including expected shortfall and its mixtures, and shows that entropic utility is computed from the same quantiles. In numerical experiments, the learned hedges approach dynamic programming references, and a single distributional critic trained without a preference can serve preferences chosen after training.

entry.title: VerifiQuant: A Framework That Governs Financial AI by Checking Each Question Before Calculating
entry.summary: VerifiQuant: Governance-by-Execution for Financial LLM Workflows arXiv · Nov 15, 2026The paper presents VerifiQuant, a framework that packages financial logic into inference contracts and runs each query through an executable diagnostic funnel before deterministic computation. Financial arithmetic is kept outside the language model, so answering, asking for clarification, and refusing are all structured and auditable. The main benefit reported is safer behavior when an input does not support a numeric answer, such as stating that no contract applies rather than guessing, rather than higher accuracy on well-posed questions.
